facts.statement: The only known specimen of Antarctopelta was discovered in 1986 by Argentine geologists Eduardo Olivero and Robert Scasso.
facts.quote: The only described specimen was found in 1986 and was the first dinosaur fossil to be named from the continent, by Argentine geologists Eduardo Olivero and Robert Scasso.

facts.statement: The genus and type species Antarctopelta oliveroi were formally described in 2006 by Leonardo Salgado and Zulma Gasparini.
facts.quote: The fossils were later described in 2006 by paleontologists Leonardo Salgado and Zulma Gasparini, who named the type species A. oliveroi after Olivero.

facts.statement: Antarctopelta is a medium-sized ankylosaur reaching at least 4 meters in length.
facts.quote: Antarctopelta is a medium-sized ankylosaur, reaching 4 m or more in length

facts.statement: The tail of Antarctopelta likely ended in a macuahuitl, a cluster of spiked osteoderms resembling an Aztec weapon.
facts.quote: Its tail likely terminated in an arrangement of spiked osteoderms known as a macuahuitl, which resembled an Aztec weapon of the same name.

facts.statement: Osteoderms covered various parts of Antarctopelta's body and existed in six different shapes, including large flat plates and tall keeled ones.
facts.quote: Osteoderms were present on other parts of the body and came in six different shapes, with some being large and flat while others were tall and keeled.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen MLP 86-X-28-1 is the only known material of the genus and species Antarctopelta.
facts.quote: The holotype (specimen used as the basis for the taxon) MLP 86-X-28-1 is the only known material of this genus and species

facts.statement: The holotype consists of approximately 15% of the skeleton, including skull fragments, vertebrae, limb bones, and armor pieces.
facts.quote: It consists of three isolated teeth, part of the lower jaw with another tooth in situ, some other skull fragments, vertebrae of the neck, back, hips and tail, some shoulder and hip bones (scapula, ilium) a thigh bone (femur), foot and hand bones (five metapodials and two phalanges), and numerous pieces of armor, representing approximately 15% of the skeleton.

facts.statement: The fossil material of Antarctopelta came from a single individual spread over an area of 6 square meters.
facts.quote: The material all came from a single individual, but was spread over a 6 m2 area and collected over several field seasons.

facts.statement: Antarctopelta was a stocky, herbivorous quadruped protected by skin-embedded armor plates.
facts.quote: Like other ankylosaurs, Antarctopelta oliveroi was a stocky, herbivorous quadruped protected by armor plates embedded in the skin.

facts.statement: Antarctopelta had a small head with jaws lined by small, leaf-shaped teeth.
facts.quote: The head was small, with jaws lined with small, leaf-shaped teeth.

facts.statement: Antarctopelta had short, roughly equal-length limbs, with five toes on the forefeet and six on the hindfeet.
facts.quote: The limbs were short and about equal in length, the forefeet having five toes while the hindfeet had six.

facts.statement: A supraorbital bone on Antarctopelta bore a short spike that would have projected outward over the eye.
facts.quote: One bone in particular, identified as a supraorbital (brow ridge bone), bore a short spike which would have projected outwards over the eye.

facts.statement: Each Antarctopelta tooth has seven to eight mesial denticles, the highest number known in Parankylosauria, distinguishing it from Stegouros.
facts.quote: Seven to eight mesial denticles are found on each Antarctopelta tooth, the highest number known from Parankylosauria, a trait distinguishing it from the related Stegouros.

facts.statement: Antarctopelta is the only known ankylosaur from Antarctica and belongs to the subfamily Parankylosauria.
facts.quote: Antarctopelta is the only known ankylosaur from Antarctica and a member of Parankylosauria.

facts.statement: Antarctopelta coexisted with the ornithopod Trinisaura, as well as mosasaurs, plesiosaurs, and sharks.
facts.quote: Antarctopelta coexisted with the ornithopod dinosaur Trinisaura in addition to a menagerie of mosasaurs, plesiosaurs, and sharks.

facts.statement: The discovery of a shark tooth and bivalves with the specimen suggests Antarctopelta died and floated out to sea, a behavior seen in other ankylosaurs.
facts.quote: At this site, the specimen was unearthed with a tooth of the shark Notidanodon, likely due to scavenging, as well as bivalves. This implies that the ankylosaur died and floated out to sea, a phenomenon observed in other ankylosaurs.

facts.statement: Five cervical vertebrae were discovered, but three were lost after being molded with latex.
facts.quote: Five cervical vertebrae were found in the field, though three were molded by latex and the originally material was subsequently lost.

facts.statement: The cervical vertebrae have short centra with biconcave ends and a length-to-height ratio of 0.57.
facts.quote: Their centra are proportionally short with amphicoelus (biconcave) ends, bearing a centrum length to height ratio of only 0.57.

facts.statement: The neural canals in the cervical vertebrae are circular and significantly larger than those found in Stegouros.
facts.quote: Neural canals, the area where the notochord would pass through, in these vertebrae are circular in cross-section and much larger than in Stegouros.

facts.statement: Two complete and one incomplete sacral vertebrae were collected, with the last one containing parts of the sacrum.
facts.quote: Two complete and one incomplete sacral vertebrae, the last of which contains parts of the sacrum, were collected as well.

facts.statement: The sacral vertebrae are firmly fused to each other and to the sacrum.
facts.quote: These vertebrae are firmly ankylosed (fused) with each other and the sacrum.

facts.statement: Eight caudal vertebrae from the middle and distal parts of the tail are preserved.
facts.quote: Eight caudal vertebrae are preserved from the middle and distal portions of the tail.

facts.statement: Ossified tendons are associated with the upper and lower sides of the distal caudal vertebrae.
facts.quote: The distal caudals are associated with ossified tendons on the upper and lower sides.

facts.statement: The term 'macuahuitl' refers to an Aztec weapon, chosen because of the tail structure's similar appearance and function.
facts.quote: The name is in reference to the Aztec weapon due to its similar appearance and function.

facts.statement: The distal end of the left femur was found among the remains.
facts.quote: The distal end of the left femur (thigh bone) was found.

facts.statement: The estimated total length of the femur is approximately 30 cm.
facts.quote: An estimate of the femur's total length was made, with an approximation of 30 cm long.

facts.statement: Five metapodials and two phalanges from the hand and possibly the foot were discovered.
facts.quote: Five metapodials and two phalanges from the manus and possibly pes were also found.

facts.statement: Like Stegouros, Antarctopelta had four digits with four metapodials on both the hand and foot.
facts.quote: Ankylosaurs like Antarctopelta and Stegouros had four digits with four metapodials on the manus and pes.

facts.statement: Fragments of the scapula and ilium were found, but the scapula was notably unfused with the coracoid.
facts.quote: Fragments from the scapula (shoulderblade) and ilium were unearthed, though the former bone is notably unfused with the coracoid.

facts.statement: Six types of osteoderms were found, but their specific placement on the body remains largely speculative due to poor articulation.
facts.quote: Six different types of osteoderms were found along with the skeletal remains of Antarctopelta, but very few were articulated with the skeleton, so their placement on the body is largely speculative.

facts.statement: One type of osteoderm included the base of a large spike.
facts.quote: They included the base of what would have been a large spike.

facts.statement: Large circular plates associated with smaller nodules may have formed a shield over the hips, similar to Sauropelta.
facts.quote: Large circular plates were found associated with smaller, polygonal nodules, perhaps forming a shield over the hips as seen in Sauropelta.

facts.statement: Some osteoderms were ossified to the ribs, suggesting they ran in rows along the flanks, a typical ankylosaur pattern.
facts.quote: A few examples of this fifth type were found ossified to the ribs, suggesting that they ran in rows along the flanks of the animal, a very typical pattern among ankylosaurs.

facts.statement: The final group of osteoderms consisted of small bony nodules called ossicles, likely scattered throughout the body.
facts.quote: The final group consisted mainly of small bony nodules which are often called ossicles, and were probably scattered throughout the body.

facts.statement: A 2011 phylogenetic analysis suggested that Antarctopelta is the most basal known nodosaurid.
facts.quote: Later, in 2011 a phylogenetic analysis performed by Thompson and colleagues suggested that Antarctopelta was the basalmost known nodosaurid.

facts.statement: In 2021, a new ankylosaur group called Parankylosauria was described, including Stegouros.
facts.quote: In 2021, Sergio Soto-Acuña and colleagues described a new group of ankylosaurs, the Parankylosauria, with the description of Stegouros.

facts.statement: The Parankylosauria clade includes Kunbarrasaurus, Stegouros, and Antarctopelta, with Antarctopelta being the largest of these small Southern Hemisphere ankylosaurs.
facts.quote: This clade minimally comprises Kunbarrasaurus, Stegouros, and Antarctopelta, all of which are small ankylosaurs from the Southern Hemisphere, the latter of which is the largest.

facts.statement: The genus Antarctopelta was named by Salgado and Gasparini in 2006.
facts.quote: genus_authority: Salgado & Gasparini, 2006.

facts.statement: The species A. oliveroi was named by Salgado and Gasparini in 2006.
facts.quote: species_authority: Salgado & Gasparini, 2006

facts.statement: Antarctopelta lived during the Late Cretaceous period.
facts.quote: fossil_range: Cretácico Superior

facts.statement: The holotype skeleton was found about 90 meters from the base of the Gamma Member of the Snow Hill Island Formation.
facts.quote: The holotype skeleton was collected about 90 m from the base of the Gamma Member of the Snow Hill Island Formation.

facts.statement: During Antarctopelta's time, Earth was warmer and humider, leaving Antarctica ice-free.
facts.quote: During the time in which Antarctopelta lived, Earth's climate was much warmer and more humid than it is today and as a result Antarctica was without ice.

facts.statement: The environment was dominated by dense conifer forests, cycads, and ginkgos.
facts.quote: The environment was mainly dominated by large dense conifer forests, cycads, and ginkgos.

facts.statement: Despite being found in marine sediment, Antarctopelta lived on land like other ankylosaurs.
facts.quote: Despite being found in marine sediment, Antarctopelta, like all ankylosaurs, lived on land.

facts.statement: Based on phylogenetic bracketing, Antarctopelta probably had a macuahuitl similar to its relative Stegouros.
facts.quote: Antarctopelta, based on phylogenetic bracketing and known material, probably had a macuahuitl like its relative Stegouros.

facts.statement: A 2019 histological analysis revealed that the holotype individual was sexually mature.
facts.quote: However, a 2019 histological analysis by Argentine paleontologist Ignacio Cerda and colleagues found that the holotype individual was sexually mature.

facts.statement: Bone growth rates in Antarctopelta remained consistent despite different climatic conditions compared to lower latitude ankylosaurs.
facts.quote: This suggests that the growth rates remained the same, despite different climatic or environmental conditions.

facts.statement: It is debated whether the individual was immature based on bone fusion, as histological analysis suggests it was sexually mature.
facts.quote: This suggests that the individual was immature, though histological analysis contradicts this.

facts.statement: Antarctopelta oliveroi is the only known species of the extinct ankylosaurian dinosaur genus.
facts.quote: Antarctopelta oliveroi (lat. "escudo de la Antártida de Eduardo Olivero") es la única especie conocida del género extinto de dinosaurio anquilosauriano

facts.quote: que vivió a finales del período Cretácico, hace aproximadamente 74 a 70 millones de años, en el Campaniense, en lo que hoy es la Antártida

facts.statement: Its leaf-shaped teeth were asymmetrical, with most denticles on the edge closer to the tip of the snout.

facts.statement: Examples of the fifth type were found ossified on the ribs, suggesting they were arranged in rows along the animal's flanks.

facts.statement: The holotype is the only known specimen of this genus and species.

facts.statement: Most of the skeleton was in poor condition because bones near the surface were subject to fragmentation by frost action over several years.

facts.statement: The genus name refers to its location on the Antarctic continent.

facts.statement: Only one species is named, A. oliveroi, in honor of Argentine geologist Eduardo Olivero, who discovered the holotype and worked in Antarctica for decades.

facts.statement: It shares traits with both ankylosaurids (tail club) and nodosaurids (teeth and armor), making family assignment difficult, so it has been designated as Ankylosauria incertae sedis.

facts.statement: A new phylogenetic analysis by Thompson et al. in 2011 suggests that Antarctopelta is the most basal known nodosaurid.

facts.statement: The holotype skeleton was collected about 90 meters from the base of the gamma member of the Snow Hill Island Formation in Antarctica, from late Campanian strata, approximately 74 to 70 million years ago.
